info.title: Runware API - FLUX.1 [dev]
info.summary: Open-weight 12B text to image model for rich visuals
info.description: FLUX.1 [dev] is a 12-billion-parameter text-to-image model from Black Forest Labs. Its guidance-distilled architecture combines strong prompt adherence with detailed, high-quality visual generation, making it a versatile foundation for creative image workflows and customized model development.

AuthenticationTask.title: Authentication
AuthenticationTask.description: Authenticates a connection using an API key. Can be sent as the first element of the request array as an alternative to using the Authorization header.

taskType.title: Task Type
taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task being performed.

connectionSessionUUID.title: Connection Session UUID
connectionSessionUUID.description: Optional session UUID to resume a previous connection and receive any buffered results.

model.title: Model
model.description: Identifier of the model to use for generation.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: Total number of denoising steps. Higher values generally produce more detailed results but take longer.

seedImage.title: Seed Image
seedImage.description: Image used as a starting point for the generation (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

maskImage.title: Mask Image
maskImage.description: Image used to specify which areas of the input image should be edited (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64). White marks the area to edit, black is preserved.

positivePrompt.title: Positive Prompt
positivePrompt.description: Text prompt describing elements to include in the generated output.

negativePrompt.title: Negative Prompt
negativePrompt.description: Prompt to guide what to exclude from generation. Ignored when guidance is disabled (CFGScale ≤ 1).

width.title: Width
width.description: Width of the generated media in pixels.

height.title: Height
height.description: Height of the generated media in pixels.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Random seed for reproducible generation. When not provided, a random seed is generated in the unsigned 32-bit range.

scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.description: Scheduler to use for the diffusion process.

CFGScale.title: CFG Scale
CFGScale.description: Guidance scale representing how closely the output will resemble the prompt. Higher values produce results more aligned with the prompt.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: Strength of the transformation. Lower values result in more influence from the original input.

maskMargin.title: Mask Margin
maskMargin.description: Extra context pixels around the masked region during inpainting. The model zooms into the masked area with these additional pixels for better integration.

promptWeighting.title: Prompt Weighting
promptWeighting.description:
Defines the syntax to be used for prompt weighting.

Prompt weighting allows you to adjust how strongly different parts of your prompt influence the generated image. Choose between `compel` notation with advanced weighting operations or `sdEmbeds` for simple emphasis adjustments.

**Compel syntax**:

Adds 0.2 seconds to image inference time and incurs additional costs.

When `compel` syntax is selected, you can use the following notation in prompts:

**Weighting**

Syntax: `+` `-` `(word)0.9`

Increase or decrease the attention given to specific words or phrases.

Examples:

- Single words: `small+ dog, pixar style`
- Multiple words: `small dog, (pixar style)-`
- Multiple symbols for more effect: `small+++ dog, pixar style`
- Nested weighting: `(small+ dog)++, pixar style`
- Explicit weight percentage: `small dog, (pixar)1.2 style`

**Blend**

Syntax: `.blend()`

Merge multiple conditioning prompts.

Example: `("small dog", "robot").blend(1, 0.8)`

**Conjunction**

Syntax: `.and()`

Break a prompt into multiple clauses and pass them separately.

Example: `("small dog", "pixar style").and()`

**SdEmbeds syntax**:

When `sdEmbeds` syntax is selected, you can use the following notation in prompts:

**Weighting**

Syntax: `(text)` `(text:number)` `[text]`

Use parentheses `()` to increase attention, square brackets `[]` to decrease it. Add a number after the text to specify a custom multiplier.

Examples:

- Single words: `(small) dog, pixar style`
- Multiple words: `small dog, [pixar style]`
- Higher emphasis: `(small:2.5) dog, pixar style`
- Combined emphasis: `(small dog:1.5), pixar style`

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#promptWeighting)

acceleratorOptions.title: Accelerator Options
acceleratorOptions.description: Advanced caching mechanisms to speed up generation.

cacheEndStep.title: Cache End Step
cacheEndStep.description: Absolute step number to end caching. Must be greater than `cacheStartStep` and less than or equal to `steps`.

cacheEndStepPercentage.title: Cache End Step Percentage
cacheEndStepPercentage.description: Percentage of steps to end caching. Alternative to `cacheEndStep`. Must be greater than `cacheStartStepPercentage`.

cacheMaxConsecutiveSteps.title: Cache Max Consecutive Steps
cacheMaxConsecutiveSteps.description: Limits the maximum number of consecutive steps that can use cached computations before forcing a fresh computation.

cacheStartStep.title: Cache Start Step
cacheStartStep.description: Absolute step number to start caching. Must be less than `cacheEndStep`.

cacheStartStepPercentage.title: Cache Start Step Percentage
cacheStartStepPercentage.description: Percentage of steps to start caching. Alternative to `cacheStartStep`. Must be less than `cacheEndStepPercentage`.

teaCache.title: TeaCache
teaCache.description: TeaCache acceleration for transformer-based models. Estimates step differences to skip redundant computations.

teaCacheDistance.title: TeaCache Distance
teaCacheDistance.description: Controls the aggressiveness of the TeaCache feature. Lower values prioritize quality, higher values prioritize speed.

dbCache.title: DB Cache
dbCache.description: DB Cache (CacheDiT) acceleration. Caches and reuses intermediate transformer block outputs to skip redundant computations.

dbCacheThreshold.title: DB Cache Threshold
dbCacheThreshold.description: Controls the sensitivity threshold for DB Cache. Lower values reuse cached blocks more aggressively, higher values prioritize quality.

dbCacheSkipInterval.title: DB Cache Skip Interval
dbCacheSkipInterval.description: Controls how many steps to skip between cache refreshes. Higher values skip more steps for faster generation at the cost of quality.

outpaint.title: Outpaint
outpaint.description: Pixel extensions for each boundary direction of the source image. At least one direction is required.

top.title: Outpaint Top
top.description: Number of pixels to extend to the top.

bottom.title: Outpaint Bottom
bottom.description: Number of pixels to extend to the bottom.

left.title: Outpaint Left
left.description: Number of pixels to extend to the left.

right.title: Outpaint Right
right.description: Number of pixels to extend to the right.

blur.title: Outpaint Blur
blur.description: Amount of blur to apply to the mask edge.

lora.title: LoRA
lora.description:
With LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), you can adapt a model to specific styles or features by emphasizing particular aspects of the data. This technique enhances the quality and relevance of generated content and can be especially useful when the output needs to adhere to a specific artistic style or follow particular guidelines.

Multiple LoRA models can be used simultaneously to achieve different adaptation goals.

**Examples**:

```json
"lora": [
  {
    "model": "<lora-model-air>",
    "weight": 0.8
  }
]
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#lora)

weight.title: LoRA Weight
weight.description: Strength of the LoRA influence. A value of 0 means no influence. Higher values increase the influence, and negative values can be used to steer away from the LoRA's style.

controlNet.title: ControlNet
controlNet.description:
With ControlNet, you can provide a guide image to help the model generate images that align with the desired structure. This guide image can be generated with our ControlNet preprocessing tool, extracting guidance information from an input image. The guide image can be in the form of an edge map, a pose, a depth estimation or any other type of control image that guides the generation process via the ControlNet model.

Multiple ControlNet models can be used at the same time to provide different types of guidance information to the model.

**Examples**:

```json
"controlNet": [
  {
    "model": "<controlnet-model-air>",
    "guideImage": "c64351d5-4c59-42f7-95e1-eace013eddab",
    "weight": 0.7,
    "startStep": 0,
    "endStep": 20,
    "controlMode": "controlnet"
  }
]
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#controlNet)

weight.title: ControlNet Weight
weight.description: Strength of the ControlNet influence. A value of 0 means no influence. Higher values increase the influence, and negative values can be used to steer away from the guide image.

guideImage.title: Guide Image
guideImage.description: Reference image for ControlNet guidance (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

oneOf.description: Equal weight between ControlNet and prompt.

endStep.title: ControlNet End Step
endStep.description: Absolute step number to end ControlNet influence. Must be greater than `startStep` and less than or equal to `steps`.

endStepPercentage.title: End Step Percentage
endStepPercentage.description: Percentage of steps to end ControlNet influence. Must be greater than `startStepPercentage`.

startStep.title: Start Step
startStep.description: Absolute step number to start ControlNet influence. Must be less than `endStep`.

startStepPercentage.title: Start Step Percentage
startStepPercentage.description: Percentage of steps to start ControlNet influence. Must be less than `endStepPercentage`.

ipAdapters.title: IP Adapters
ipAdapters.description:
IP-Adapters enable image-prompted generation, allowing you to use reference images to guide the style and content of your generations. Multiple IP Adapters can be used simultaneously.

**Examples**:

```json
"ipAdapters": [
  {
    "model": "<ip-adapter-model-air>",
    "guideImages": ["c64351d5-4c59-42f7-95e1-eace013eddab"],
    "weight": 0.75
  },
  {
    "model": "<ip-adapter-model-air>",
    "guideImages": ["d7e8f9a0-2b5c-4e7f-a1d3-9c8b7a6e5d4f"],
    "weight": 0.5
  }
]
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#ipAdapters)

model.title: IP-Adapter Model
model.description:
We make use of the [AIR system](https://runware.ai/docs/models) to identify IP-Adapter models. This identifier is a unique string that represents a specific model.

**Supported models list**:

| AIR ID | Model Name |

| runware:55@1 | IP Adapter SDXL |
| runware:55@2 | IP Adapter SDXL Plus |
| runware:55@3 | IP Adapter SDXL Plus Face |
| runware:55@4 | IP Adapter SDXL Vit-H |
| runware:55@5 | IP Adapter SD 1.5 |
| runware:55@6 | IP Adapter SD 1.5 Plus |
| runware:55@7 | IP Adapter SD 1.5 Light |
| runware:55@8 | IP Adapter SD 1.5 Plus Face |
| runware:55@10 | IP Adapter SD 1.5 Vit-G |

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#model)

weight.title: IP-Adapter Weight
weight.description: Strength of the IP-Adapter influence. A value of 0 means no influence. Higher values increase the influence, and negative values can be used to steer away from the reference.

guideImages.title: Guide Images
guideImages.description: Images to guide the IP-Adapter (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

items.title: Image
items.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

layerDiffuse.title: Layer Diffuse
layerDiffuse.description:
Enables LayerDiffuse technology, which allows for the direct generation of images with transparency (alpha channels).

When enabled, this feature applies the necessary LwwwwwwoRA and VAE components to produce high-quality transparent images without requiring post-processing background removal.

This is particularly useful for creating product images, overlays, composites, and other content that requires transparency. The output must be in a format that supports transparency, such as PNG.

Note: This feature is only available for the FLUX model architecture. It automatically applies the equivalent of:

```json

  "lora": [{ "model": "runware:120@2" }],
  "vae": "runware:120@4"
```

**Examples**:

```json
"outputFormat": "png",
"advancedFeatures": {
  "layerDiffuse": true
}
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#layerDiffuse)

watermark.title: Watermark

image.title: Watermark Image
image.description: Watermark image (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

hiresFix.title: HiresFix
hiresFix.description:
Two-stage generation for improved resolution and detail. The model generates at a lower resolution first, then upscales and refines the result in a second pass. Can be enabled with `true` for default settings, or configured as an object for fine-grained control over the upscaling model, steps, and strength.

When using the object form, the `model` parameter is required. Available upscaling models:

| Model | Name | Upscale Factor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runware:504@1` | RealESRGAN\_x4plus | 4x |
| `runware:realesrgan@anime-6b` | RealESRGAN\_x4plus\_anime\_6B | 4x |
| `runware:esrgan@animesharp` | 4x-AnimeSharp | 4x |
| `runware:esrgan@ultrasharp` | 4x-UltraSharp | 4x |

**Simple (boolean)**:

```json
"hiresFix": true
```

**Configured (object)**:

```json
"hiresFix": {
  "model": "runware:esrgan@ultrasharp",
  "steps": 15,
  "strength": 0.6
}
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#hiresFix)

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: Total number of denoising steps. Higher values generally produce more detailed results but take longer.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: Strength of the transformation. Lower values result in more influence from the original input.

upscaleFactor.title: Upscale Factor
upscaleFactor.description: Factor by which to upscale the generated image. A value of 2 doubles width and height.

pulid.title: PuLID
pulid.description:
PuLID (Pure and Lightning ID Customization) enables fast and high-quality identity customization for text-to-image generation. This object allows you to configure settings for transferring facial characteristics from a reference image to generated images with high fidelity.

> [!NOTE]
> `CFGstartStep` and `CFGstartStepPercentage` are mutually exclusive, they both control when CFG guidance begins, but as an absolute step number or a percentage respectively. Use one or the other, not both.

**Examples**:

```json
"puLID": {
  "images": ["59a2edc2-45e6-429f-be5f-7ded59b92046"],
  "idWeight": 1,
  "trueCFGScale": 1.5,
  "CFGStartStep": 3
}
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#pulid)

CFGstartStep.title: CFG Start Step
CFGstartStep.description: Absolute step number to start identity influence. Must be less than `steps`.

CFGstartStepPercentage.title: CFG Start Step Percentage
CFGstartStepPercentage.description: Percentage of steps to start identity influence.

idWeight.title: ID Weight
idWeight.description: Identity preservation strength. Higher values create closer resemblance to the reference face.

images.title: Images
images.description: Reference images for identity customization (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

items.title: Image
items.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

trueCFGScale.title: True CFG Scale
trueCFGScale.description: True Classifier-Free Guidance scale. Higher values increase prompt adherence at the cost of quality.

ultralytics.title: Ultralytics Features
ultralytics.description:
Configuration object for Ultralytics face enhancement during generation. This feature uses face detection and inpainting to improve facial details in the same generation step, without requiring post-processing.

> [!NOTE]
> Face enhancement is available for Stable Diffusion 1.X, SDXL, and FLUX models. The system automatically detects faces and applies targeted refinement to improve quality while maintaining consistency with the overall generation.

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#ultralytics)

inpaintSize.title: Inpaint Size
inpaintSize.description: Image size (in pixels) to use for each inpainting region. YOLO detects faces, crops the region, and scales it to this size before running diffusion. Set so most faces land in the 2–4× range of their original pixel size. Going beyond 8× may degrade identity resemblance.

maskBlur.title: Mask Blur
maskBlur.description: Mask feathering amount. Higher values create softer transitions between the enhanced face region and surrounding areas.

maskPadding.title: Mask Padding
maskPadding.description: Padding around detected face in pixels. Expands the refinement area to include surrounding context like hair and neck.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: Refinement strength. Lower values preserve more of the original, higher values allow more aggressive reconstruction.

taskType.title: Task Type
taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task being performed.

taskUUID.title: Task UUID
taskUUID.description: UUID v4 identifier for tracking tasks and matching async responses. Must be unique per task.

webhookURL.title: Webhook URL
webhookURL.description: Webhook URL that receives JSON responses via HTTP POST when generation tasks complete. For batch requests with multiple results, each completed item triggers a separate webhook call as it becomes available.

includeCost.title: Include Cost
includeCost.description: Include task cost in the response.

numberResults.title: Number of Results
numberResults.description: Number of results to generate. Each result uses a different seed, producing variations of the same parameters.

uploadEndpoint.title: Upload Endpoint
uploadEndpoint.description:
Specifies a URL where the generated content will be automatically uploaded using the HTTP PUT method. The raw binary data of the media file is sent directly as the request body. For secure uploads to cloud storage, use presigned URLs that include temporary authentication credentials.

**Common use cases:**

- **Cloud storage**: Upload directly to S3 buckets, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage using presigned URLs.
- **CDN integration**: Upload to content delivery networks for immediate distribution.

```text
// S3 presigned URL for secure upload
https://your-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/generated/content.mp4?X-Amz-Signature=abc123&X-Amz-Expires=3600

// Google Cloud Storage presigned URL
https://storage.googleapis.com/your-bucket/content.jpg?X-Goog-Signature=xyz789

// Custom storage endpoint
https://storage.example.com/uploads/generated-image.jpg
```

The content data will be sent as the request body to the specified URL when generation is complete.

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#uploadEndpoint)

ttl.title: TTL
ttl.description: Time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for generated content. Only applies when `outputType` is `URL`.

outputFormat.title: Output Format
outputFormat.description:
Specifies the file format of the generated output. The available values depend on the task type and the specific model's capabilities.

- \`JPG\`: Best for photorealistic images with smaller file sizes (no transparency).
- \`PNG\`: Lossless compression, supports high quality and transparency (alpha channel).
- \`WEBP\`: Modern format providing superior compression and transparency support.
- \`MP4\`: Widely supported video container (H.264), recommended for general use.
- \`WEBM\`: Optimized for web delivery.
- \`MOV\`: QuickTime format, common in professional workflows (Apple ecosystem).
- \`GIF\`: Animated image format (no audio), suitable for short loops or previews.
- \`MP3\`: Compressed audio, smaller file size.
- \`WAV\`: Uncompressed, high-quality audio.
- \`FLAC\`: Lossless compression.
- \`OGG\`: Open-source compressed audio format (Vorbis codec).
- \`SVG\`: Scalable Vector Graphics.
- \`TIFF\`: High-quality output supporting layers.
- \`GLB\`: Binary glTF format for 3D models, including geometry, textures, and PBR materials.

> [!NOTE]
> \*\*Transparency\*\*: If you are using features like background removal or LayerDiffuse that require transparency, you must select a format that supports an alpha channel (e.g., \`PNG\`, \`WEBP\`, \`TIFF\`). \`JPG\` does not support transparency.

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/bfl-flux-1-dev#outputFormat)

outputQuality.title: Output Quality
outputQuality.description: Compression quality of the output. Higher values preserve quality but increase file size.

deliveryMethod.title: Delivery Method
deliveryMethod.description: Determines how the API delivers task results.

oneOf.description: Returns complete results directly in the API response.
Returns an immediate acknowledgment with the task UUID. Poll for results using getResponse.

safety.title: Safety Settings
safety.description: Content safety checking configuration for image generation.

checkContent.title: Check Content
checkContent.description: Enable or disable content safety checking. Increases total generation time.

RequestBody.description: You must always POST an array of task objects.

taskType.title: Task Type
taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task this response belongs to.

taskUUID.title: Task UUID
taskUUID.description: UUID v4 identifier echoed from the original request, used to match async responses to their tasks.

cost.title: Cost
cost.description: Task cost in USD. Present when `includeCost` is set to `true` in the request.

imageDataURI.title: Image Data URI
imageDataURI.description: Data URI of the output image.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: The seed used for generation. If none was provided, shows the randomly generated seed.

NSFWContent.title: NSFW Content
NSFWContent.description: Flag indicating if NSFW content was detected.

ErrorResponse.title: Error Response
ErrorResponse.description: Standard error response returned by the Runware API.

code.description: A short identifier for the error (e.g., invalidApiKey, timeoutProvider).

message.description: A human-readable explanation of what went wrong.

parameter.description: The request parameter related to the error, if applicable.

taskType.description: The task type of the request that failed.

taskUUID.description: The unique identifier of the failed request.

400.description: Bad Request — Missing or invalid parameters.

401.description: Unauthorized — No valid API key provided.

403.description: Forbidden — The API key lacks permissions for this request.

429.description: Too Many Requests — Rate limit exceeded.

500.description: Server Error — Something went wrong on Runware's end.

503.description: Service Unavailable — Temporarily unavailable (maintenance or capacity).
